the annealing at 873 K led to the formation of a recrystallized equiaxed very fine-grained structure with average grain size approximately 9 µm
annealing at 1073 K resulted in considerably coarse-grained equiaxed structure with average grain size approximately 58 µm
annealing at 1273 K led to extremely rapid grain growth, resulting in coarse-grained structure with average grain size approximately 263 µm, wherein the grain size varied in the range of 100 –500 µm
an annealing at 1273 K results in the development of a speci ﬁc preferential crystallographic texture in the cold rolled specimens
the cold rolling does result in significant strengthening due to strain hardening owing to the accumulation of abundance of defects
The average hardness of the as received materials was experimentally found to be approximately 213 ± 13 Hv
the average hardness of the specimens increased from 213 ± 13 Hv (2.089 ± 0.255 GPa) to 267 ± 9.8 Hv (2.618 ± 0.193 GPa) as a result of cold rolling
the average hardness further increased significantly after annealing at 673 K, leading to an average hardness value 337 ± 10 Hv (3.305 ± 0.196 GPa)

subsequent annealing to higher temperatures, i.e. 873 K, 1073 K, and 1273 K, resulted in a decreased average hardness values, which are almost similar to that of as received Ti-Nb-Zr material, i.e. of the order of 220 Hv (2.158 GPa)
